claim: In response to an osmotic challenge, the synthesis of the antidiuretic hormone arginine vasopressin (AVP) increases in the hypothalamus.

evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known phenomenon that forms the basis for the study.

claim: Osmotic challenge is accompanied by extension of the 3′ poly(A) tail of the AVP mRNA.

evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Carrazana et al., 1988; Zingg et al., 1988; Carter and Murphy, 1989; Murphy and Carter, 1990).

claim: Osmotic challenge is accompanied by up-regulation of the expression of RNA binding protein Caprin-2.

claim: Caprin-2 binds to AVP mRNAs.

claim: Lentiviral mediated shRNA knockdown of Caprin-2 in the osmotically stimulated hypothalamus shortens the AVP mRNA poly(A) tail.

claim: The HNS is the source of the antidiuretic neuropeptide hormone arginine vasopressin (AVP).

claim: The HNS consists of the large peptidergic magnocellular neurones (MCNs) of the hypothalamic supraoptic nuclei (SON) and paraventricular nuclei (PVN).

claim: The axons of MCNs course through the internal zone of the median eminence and terminate on blood capillaries of the posterior pituitary (PP) gland.

claim: The biosynthesis of AVP starts with the translation of AVP-encoding mRNAs into a large precursor preprohormone.

claim: Caprin-2 knockdown significantly reduced Caprin-2 mRNA level in HEK293T cells (Ctrl, 1.00 ± 0.03 vs Cap2 KD, 0.13 ± 0.01, n = 5, p ≤ 0.0001).

source: whilst overexpression increases (Ctrl, 804.4 ± 6.19 nt. vs Caprin-2, 884.3 ± 5.51 nt., n = 5; p ≤ 0.0001) the length of the AVP mRNA.

evidence: This is stated in the Figure 9 legend and shown in Figure 9B and F.

claim: Caprin-2 plays a critical role in mediating brain responses to osmotic stress.
source: We provide the first evidence that RNA binding protein Caprin-2 plays a critical role in mediating brain responses to osmotic stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Caprin-2 is expressed in AVP MCNs in the SON and PVN.
source: We show that Caprin-2 is expressed in AVP MCNs in the SON and PVN
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2.

claim: Caprin-2 expression in AVP MCNs increases during osmotic stress.
source: and that Caprin-2 expression in these neurons increases during osmotic stress.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Caprin-2 knockdown in the SON and PVN disrupts physiological osmoregulatory mechanisms.
source: Importantly, we demonstrate that Caprin-2 knockdown in the SON and PVN disrupts physiological osmoregulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by physiological data in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: Loss of Caprin-2 significantly reduces the salt loading-induced urine output and fluid intake.
source: Loss of Caprin-2 significantly reduces the salt loading-induced urine output and fluid intake and increases urine osmolality, urine sodium concentration and plasma AVP levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: Loss of Caprin-2 increases urine osmolality, urine sodium concentration and plasma AVP levels.
source: Loss of Caprin-2 significantly reduces the salt loading-induced urine output and fluid intake and increases urine osmolality, urine sodium concentration and plasma AVP levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: Caprin-2 has recently been identified in vitro as an RNA binding protein RNG140.
source: Caprin-2 has recently been identified in vitro as an RNA binding protein RNG140 (Shiina and Tokunaga, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Up until now, no specific RNA binding partners of Caprin-2 have been identified.
source: However, up until now, no specific RNA binding partners of Caprin-2 have been identified.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as context for the novelty of the findings.

claim: Caprin-2 binds to the AVP mRNA in the SON and PVN of euhydrated and salt-loaded rats in vivo.
source: Here we show that Caprin-2 binds to the AVP mRNA in the SON and PVN of EU and SL rats in vivo, and, in doing so, modulates both its abundance and poly(A) tail length.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by RNA immunoprecipitation data in Figure 5.

claim: Caprin-2 binding to AVP mRNA modulates both its abundance and poly(A) tail length.
source: Here we show that Caprin-2 binds to the AVP mRNA in the SON and PVN of EU and SL rats in vivo, and, in doing so, modulates both its abundance and poly(A) tail length.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figures 4, 6, 8, and 9.

claim: AVP plays a central role in the maintenance of cardiovascular homeostasis, particularly blood volume and osmolality.
source: By stimulating water retention at the level of the kidneys (Breyer and Ando, 1994), AVP plays a central role in the maintenance of cardiovascular homeostasis, particularly blood volume and osmolality (Antunes-Rodrigues et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: The increase in AVP biosynthesis in MCNs that follows osmotic stimulation is accompanied by a plethora of changes in gene expression.
source: The increase in AVP biosynthesis in MCNs that follows osmotic stimulation is accompanied by a plethora of changes in gene expression (Mutsuga et al., 2004; Hindmarch et al., 2006; Yue et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Caprin-2 was one of the novel genes identified as up-regulated by transcriptome analysis following osmotic challenge.
source: One of the novel genes identified as such by transcriptome analysis was Caprin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations (Mutsuga et al., 2004; Hindmarch et al., 2006; Yue et al., 2006).

claim: Caprin-2 is up-regulated at the mRNA level by chronic hyperosmotic cues.
source: Here we confirm the transcriptome data, and that Caprin-2 protein is up-regulated at the mRNA level by chronic hyperosmotic cues.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 1.

claim: Caprin-2 protein is present in the cytoplasm of AVP MCNs.
source: Using double immunostaining we also provide evidence that Caprin-2 protein is present in the cytoplasm of VP MCNs, and that its expression increases during osmotic stress.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2.

claim: Caprin-2 protein expression increases during osmotic stress.
source: Using double immunostaining we also provide evidence that Caprin-2 protein is present in the cytoplasm of VP MCNs, and that its expression increases during osmotic stress.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by immunohistochemistry data in Figure 2.

claim: Caprin-2 has been reported to play a role in several physiological processes, including differentiation, apoptosis in erythroblasts or lens fiber cells, and synaptic plasticity in the mouse cerebellum.
source: Caprin-2 has been reported to play a role in several physiological processes, including differentiation, apoptosis in erythroblasts or lens fiber cells, and synaptic plasticity in the mouse cerebellum (Aerbajinai et al., 2004; Ding et al., 2008; Lorén et al., 2009; Shiina and Tokunaga, 2010; Miao et al., 2014; Flores and Zhong, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Expression of Caprin-2 in the HNS has been reported.
source: Although expression of Caprin-2 in the HNS has been reported (Mutsuga et al., 2004), its role in the maintenance of fluid homeostasis had not previously been addressed.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: The role of Caprin-2 in the maintenance of fluid homeostasis had not previously been addressed.
source: Although expression of Caprin-2 in the HNS has been reported (Mutsuga et al., 2004), its role in the maintenance of fluid homeostasis had not previously been addressed.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as context for the novelty of the study.

claim: The Caprin-2 shRNA had no effect on water homeostasis in euhydrated rats.
source: The Caprin-2 shRNA had no effect on water homeostasis in euhydrated rats.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: In naïve rats and in rats transduced with a scrambled control shRNA, salt loading results in production of large amounts of dilute urine and excessive fluid intake.
source: In naïve rats (Greenwood et al., 2015), and in rats transduced with a scrambled control shRNA, as shown here, salt loading results in production of large amounts of dilute urine and excessive fluid intake.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 4 and Table 1, with citation support.

claim: Compared to the control animals, salt loaded Caprin-2 knockdown rats only minimally increased their urine production and they drank less fluid.
source: However, compared to the control animals, salt loaded Caprin-2 knockdown rats only minimally increased their urine production and they drank less fluid.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: Urine osmolality and sodium levels were higher in Caprin-2 knockdown rats.
source: Urine osmolality and sodium levels were also higher in Caprin-2 knockdown rats.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 4 and Table 1.

claim: The elevated plasma AVP levels found in the Caprin-2 shRNA-transduced rats may explain the observed changes in urine production and fluid intake.
source: These observations may be explained by water retention resulting from the elevated plasma AVP levels found in the Caprin-2 shRNA-transduced rats.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Caprin-2 knockdown rats increase their ability to concentrate urine.
source: Our data suggest that Caprin-2 knockdown rats increase their ability to concentrate urine and so doing they prevent the decrease in sodium excretion (i.e., elevation of plasma sodium) resulting from lower urine output by producing more concentrated urine.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Caprin-2 binding to AVP mRNA may be important for stabilization of AVP mRNAs during osmotic stress.
source: The direct binding and positive regulation of AVP transcript levels suggest that Caprin-2 may be important for stabilization of AVP mRNAs during osmotic stress, in a similar way to another AVP mRNA binding protein, poly(A)-binding protein (PABP) (Mohr et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation based on the data and comparison to PABP.

claim: One of the functions of Caprin-2-mediated poly(A) tail length regulation may be protection of AVP transcripts from degradation, which would lead to increased AVP mRNA levels.
source: It is therefore possible that one of the functions of Caprin-2-mediated poly(A) tail length regulation is protection of AVP transcripts from degradation, which in turn would lead to the observed increase of AVP mRNA levels.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation based on the data and known roles of poly(A) tails.

claim: An important role of poly(A) tail length in regulation of mRNA degradation and stability has been demonstrated for many transcripts.
source: An important role of poly(A) tail length in regulation of mRNA degradation and stability has been demonstrated for many transcripts (Curinha et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Caprin-2 binding to AVP mRNA might inhibit translation.
source: Firstly, Caprin-2 binding to AVP mRNA might inhibit translation, a phenomenon observed as a consequence of other association mRNA-RNA-binding protein interactions, such as the binding of PABP to the AVP mRNA (Mohr et al., 2002; Richter, 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis to explain the paradoxical findings, with citation support.

claim: Recombinant Caprin-2 inhibits the translation of a luciferase mRNA in a cell-free rabbit reticulocyte lysate system.
source: It has been shown previously that recombinant Caprin-2 inhibits the translation of a luciferase mRNA in a cell-free rabbit reticulocyte lysate system (Shiina and Tokunaga, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Caprin-2 knockdown in the SON and PVN may increase circulating plasma AVP levels by increasing the translation of AVP mRNA.
source: This is consistent with our observation that Caprin-2 knockdown in the SON and PVN increases circulating plasma AVP levels. It is conceivable that this effect results from the increased translation of AVP mRNA under conditions when Caprin-2 protein level is too low to suppress this process.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation to explain the findings.

claim: Knockdown of Caprin-2, whilst increasing the translation of the AVP mRNA, might increase its turnover, and hence decreases steady state transcript levels and poly(A) tail length.
source: Moreover, knockdown of Caprin-2, whilst increasing the translation of the AVP mRNA, might increase its turnover, and hence decreases steady state transcript levels and poly(A) tail length.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation to explain the findings.

claim: Polysome analysis showed no difference in the pattern of AVP mRNA association with heavy polysome fractions between euhydrated and salt-loaded SON.
source: We have previously examined the polysome distribution of the AVP mRNA in euhydrated and salt-loaded SON (Murphy and Carter, 1990), and showed no difference in the pattern association with heavy polysome fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: The rates of translation initiation, elongation and termination could be influenced, positively or negatively, by poly(A) tail length.
source: Thus, the rates of translation initiation, elongation and termination, none of which are directly measured by polysome analysis, especially when the size of the RNA limits ribosome number, could be influenced, positively or negatively, by poly(A) tail length.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation about potential mechanisms.

claim: Salt-loading elicits a significant increase in Caprin-2 protein but a significant decrease in AVP in SON neurons.
source: Quantification of Caprin-2 and AVP levels in AVP in the SON neurons (Figure 2) revealed that salt-loading elicits a significant increase in the former protein, but a significant decrease in the latter, consistent with Caprin-2 being an inhibitor of the translation of the AVP mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The steady-state level of AVP in hypothalamic MCNs is not only determined by translation rate.
source: However, it is important to point out the steady-state level of AVP in hypothalamic MCNs is not only determined by translation rate.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a caveat to the interpretation.

claim: The AVP precursor is subject to axonal transport from cell bodies in the hypothalamus to terminals in the PP.
source: As we describe in some detail in the Introduction, the AVP precursor is subject to axonal transport from cell bodies in the hypothalamus to terminals in the PP, a process that is activated by the need to deliver mature peptide to the circulation following an osmotic stimulus.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion, referring back to information in the Introduction.

claim: The effects observed after Caprin-2 knockdown could be modulated by changes in dendritic release of AVP.
source: A second, but not mutually exclusive hypothesis is that the effects that we observe after Caprin-2 knockdown could be modulated by changes in dendritic release of AVP.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an alternative hypothesis.

claim: Dendritic release and autocrine or paracrine action of AVP has been well documented.
source: Dendritic release and autocrine or paracrine action of AVP has been well documented (Ludwig and Stern, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: AVP released from dendrites inhibits the electrical activity of AVP neurons, thus suppressing axonal release to the blood stream.
source: AVP released from dendrites inhibits the electrical activity of AVP neurons, thus suppressing axonal release to the blood stream (Ludwig and Stern, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Caprin-2 protein is present in the RNA granules localized in the rat neuronal dendrites.
source: Caprin-2 protein is present in the RNA granules localized in the rat neuronal dendrites (Shiina and Tokunaga, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Caprin-2 knockdown may result in a decrease of the synthesis and dendritic release of AVP, which in turn decreases AVP-mediated auto-inhibition of AVP neurons and leads to an increase of AVP release in the neurohypophysis and increased plasma concentration.
source: Therefore, it is possible that Caprin-2 knockdown results in a decrease of the synthesis and dendritic release of AVP, which in turn decreases AVP-mediated auto-inhibition of AVP neurons and leads to an increase of AVP release in the neurohypophysis and increased plasma concentration, as we observe after Caprin-2 knockdown in the SON and PVN.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation to explain the findings.

claim: During an osmotic stimulus, the abundance of Caprin-2 protein/AVP mRNA complexes increases.
source: In this report, we have shown that, during an osmotic stimulus, three things happen to the AVP mRNA in the SON and PVN due to the action of Caprin-2: the abundance of Caprin-2 protein/AVP mRNA complexes increases, the AVP mRNA poly(A) tail elongates, and there is an increase in steady state levels of the AVP mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of findings, supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: During an osmotic stimulus, the AVP mRNA poly(A) tail elongates due to the action of Caprin-2.
source: In this report, we have shown that, during an osmotic stimulus, three things happen to the AVP mRNA in the SON and PVN due to the action of Caprin-2: the abundance of Caprin-2 protein/AVP mRNA complexes increases, the AVP mRNA poly(A) tail elongates, and there is an increase in steady state levels of the AVP mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of findings, supported by data in Figures 6 and 9.

claim: During an osmotic stimulus, there is an increase in steady state levels of the AVP mRNA due to the action of Caprin-2.
source: In this report, we have shown that, during an osmotic stimulus, three things happen to the AVP mRNA in the SON and PVN due to the action of Caprin-2: the abundance of Caprin-2 protein/AVP mRNA complexes increases, the AVP mRNA poly(A) tail elongates, and there is an increase in steady state levels of the AVP mRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of findings, supported by data in Figures 1, 4, and 8.

claim: A chronic osmotic stimulus results in an increase in the transcription of the AVP gene.
source: Whilst it has previously been demonstrated that a chronic osmotic stimulus results in an increase in the transcription of the AVP gene (Murphy and Carter, 1990), the data presented here provides new evidence that post-transcriptional process, governed by Caprin-2, are also operative.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: Post-transcriptional processes governed by Caprin-2 are operative during osmotic stimulation.
source: Whilst it has previously been demonstrated that a chronic osmotic stimulus results in an increase in the transcription of the AVP gene (Murphy and Carter, 1990), the data presented here provides new evidence that post-transcriptional process, governed by Caprin-2, are also operative.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Both transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms contribute to overall steady-state AVP mRNA abundance.
source: Both the transcriptional and the post-transcriptional mechanisms would contribute to overall steady-state AVP mRNA abundance.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: The increase in AVP mRNA mediated by Caprin-2 does not result in an increase in AVP peptide production.
source: However, it would appear that the increase in AVP mRNA mediated by Caprin-2 does not result in an increase in AVP peptide production.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the paradoxical findings.

claim: Association with Caprin-2 may inhibit the production of AVP peptide, perhaps by directly interfering with the translational apparatus, or through sequestration of AVP mRNA in translationally inert mRNP storage or transport granules.
source: Thus we suggest that association with Caprin-2 may inhibit the production of AVP peptide, perhaps by directly interfering with the translational apparatus, or through sequestration of AVP mRNA in translationally inert mRNP storage or transport granules (Buchan, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a speculation with citation support.

claim: Polysome analysis revealed a heavy class of EDTA-resistant AVP mRNA containing fractions that might represent storage granules.
source: Interestingly, polysome analysis revealed a heavy class of EDTA-resistant AVP mRNA containing fractions that might represent storage granules (Murphy and Carter, 1990).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: AVP transcripts are known to be transported to dendrites.
source: We also note that AVP transcripts are known to be transported to dendrites (Mohr et al., 2002) and to axons (Murphy et al., 1989)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: AVP transcripts are known to be transported to axons.
source: We also note that AVP transcripts are known to be transported to dendrites (Mohr et al., 2002) and to axons (Murphy et al., 1989)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: AVP RNAs in axons are characterised by a short poly(A) tail that does not change in length following osmotic stimulation.
source: although in the latter case, the AVP RNAs are characterised by a short poly(A) tail that does not change in length following osmotic stimulation (Murphy et al., 1989).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: The osmotic status-dependent modulation of AVP mRNA poly(A) tail length in the SON and PVN was first described over 20 years ago.
source: The osmotic status-dependent modulation of AVP mRNA poly(A) tail length in the SON and PVN was first described over 20 years ago (Carrazana et al., 1988; Zingg et al., 1988; Carter and Murphy, 1989)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.

claim: With the discovery of Caprin-2, we now have insight into the regulation and physiological function of AVP mRNA poly(A) tail modulation.
source: but only now, with the discovery of Caprin-2, do we have insight into the regulation and physiological function of this post-transcriptional process.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion about the significance of the findings.

claim: Similar to mouse Caprin-2, the rat Caprin-2 gene consists of 18 coding exons.
source: We found that, similar to mouse Caprin-2 (ENSMUST00000111569), the rat Caprin-2 gene consists of 18 coding exons (Supplementary file 1; Genbank accession number—KT867373).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The longest isoform of rat Caprin-2 was 3090 bp long, which encodes 1029 amino acids.
source: We found that the longest isoform was 3090 bp long, which encodes 1029 aa.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Four other isoforms of rat Caprin-2 were identified, which are shorter than the longest isoform due to the absence of several base pairs or removal of entire exons.
source: We then identified four other isoforms, which are shorter than the first one due to the absence of several base pairs (Cap2-2), or to the removal of entire exons (E13 and 14 in Cap2-3, E17 in Cap2-4, E13 in Cap2-5) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Rat Caprin-2 shares several domains with Xenopus RNG105, including N-terminal coiled-coil domain thought to be involved in RNA binding, a nuclear localization signal, and a C-terminal RNA-binding motif, RGG.
source: Comparison of the rat 3090 bp Caprin-2 sequence to the Xenopus RNG105 revealed that they share several domains, including N-terminal coiled-coil domain thought to be involved in RNA binding, a nuclear localization signal, as well as a C-terminal RNA-binding motif, RGG (Supplementary file 1) also reported to be present in human Caprin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Some MCNs express Caprin-2 but not AVP, possibly representing MCNs that express the closely related oxytocin neuropeptide hormone.
source: We note that some MCNs express Caprin-2 but not AVP. These are possibly MCNs that express the closely related oxytocin neuropeptide hormone.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation and speculation.

claim: A correlation between the length of poly(A) tail and translational activity is not always present.
source: This is not necessarily in disagreement with the fact that Caprin-2 stimulates extension of poly(A) tail in AVP mRNAs—recent studies have revealed that a correlation between the length of poly(A) tail and translational activity is not always present (Weill et al., 2012; Subtelny et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citation support.
